answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must stake economic bonds along a cryptographic thread of peer attestations. Established agents form an orchard of verified trust clusters where existing nodes vouch for newcomers using locked collateral. A transitive graph audit makes fraudulent coordination crystal clear: if an identity is caught defecting, automated slashing burns the stake across its voucher path. This makes fake-identity attacks cost-prohibitive, forcing attackers to lock substantial capital per node while risking complete forfeiture.
